newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks open down as rate cut hopes fade.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks open down as rate cut hopes fade.

text.p: Australian shares opened easier on Thursday, the market drifting after the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) dampened expectations of a rate cut in its quarterly bulletin on Monday.
At 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 5.3 points lower at 2,359.6.
The December share price index was down nine points at 2,378 and at a 18.4 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said interest rate sensitive stocks like banks and transport issues were most affected by early selling, while a large number of issues were ex-dividend today.

"At the moment it is a combination of weaker bank issues and stocks ex-dividend that is holding the market down but the signs are it could bounce back later in the session on resource buying," a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage said.
The dealer said the big miners, BHP, CRA and WMC all opened slightly lower but quickly found support and had the potential to lift the market to a record high close.

Amongst the weaker issues were all the major banks and key transport issues Brambles and Mayne Nickless. Dealers said transport stocks were also under pressure because of the recent rise in the price of oil.
In other trade the shares of food and beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil continued to slide following a broker's sell recommendation on Tuesday.
At 12.10 p.m. (0210 GMT), Coca-Cola Amatil shares were 30 cents weaker at A$17.15 (US$13.58).
